static_traits.name: An Yu
static_traits.educational_background: Currently studying for a bachelor's degree
static_traits.social_status: Having one good friend, but not yet sharing academic troubles with others
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no past psychotherapy or mental health visits
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, acceptable logic, willing to cooperate, frequent negative automatic thoughts and catastrophic inferences; speech pace not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: I recently failed my math exam, which overwhelmed me; I always feel I will therefore never be able to graduate from university.
basic_info.core_demands: Fear and negative thoughts have begun to affect my daily functioning and mental health, so I hope to resolve these problems through counseling.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough, will disappoint my family

special_situations.event: Receiving a failing grade in the math exam
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Failing one exam means I will keep failing, unable to graduate
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Immediately doubling study and considering hiring a tutor, trying to quickly recover grades
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never be able to graduate from university.

special_situations.event: When thinking of academic prospects and upcoming exams
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot do well in all future exams, it means I am just a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids deep thinking and planning; easily distracted and procrastinates when studying
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will keep failing, all exams will be failed.

special_situations.event: Situations of talking with family or classmates about exams and grades
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If grades are not good, I will disappoint my family, meaning I cannot do it
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Distancing from friends and family, reduced socializing to avoid evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I disappointed my family, they will look down on me.

special_situations.event: While self-studying other subjects alone, constantly recalling that failure
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only achieving perfect grades counts as qualified; otherwise it is complete failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeated self-criticism, compulsive intensified study yet hard to sustain focus
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I do not learn well this time either, it proves I am a total failure.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to gain family approval and acceptance through academic success
core_conflict.fear: Fear that failure will lead to family disappointment and negation, thus losing self-worth
defense_goal: Avoiding others' disappointed evaluations through distancing and not sharing feelings; maintaining a sense of control and lowering anxiety through redoubled learning and problem-solving

object_relations.self_representation: A potential failure who would disappoint family
object_relations.object_representation: Family/others with high expectations who may be disappointed and critical

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes trying new strategies (such as hiring a tutor, joining a study group) and invites them to act
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client tends to connect any attempt with total future failure, believing once something does not work it proves he cannot do it
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Acknowledging his worries in a gentle, concrete tone, inviting him to change 'big failure' to 'small experiment', using step-by-step plans and testable goals, reducing judgmental language.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to tell friends or family about feelings and stress and seek support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes expressing needs will burden others, so I must press my own needs down
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing mutual aid and the two-way nature of relationships, normalizing 'asking for help' in an empathic tone, encouraging small-step attempts to share one concrete, bearable trouble.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about exam grades and graduation prospects
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Seeing results as all good or all bad, equating one failure with total destruction of the future
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using gentle reality-testing, guiding him to identify gray areas and middle ground, using concrete data and staged goals to hedge 'all-or-nothing' thinking.

manifestations: Alienates friends and family due to stress and feelings of failure
Not yet sharing academic worries with others, worried about burdening others
Interprets one failure as a ruined future, losing hope about graduating
outcomes: Rising sense of helplessness and despair

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently using self-demands like 'I should not trouble others'
Taking 'must not fail' as a hard rule

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessive worry about disappointing family, harsh on oneself
Reduced socializing and help-seeking from fear of being judged

positive_force: Willing to seek help (tries asking classmates for help, considers hiring a tutor and study groups)
Has a degree of willingness to solve problems; willing to cooperate in making plans and trying small goals
Has one close friend; potential social support can be mobilized
negative_force: Catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking are prominent, tending to overgeneralize and predict the worst
Strong fear of failure and worry about disappointing family
Social withdrawal leading to decreased support
Sleep and diet disturbance, further weakening focus and learning motivation

target_behavior.behavior: Academic anxiety and catastrophic automatic thoughts (like 'I will never be able to graduate')
antecedent: Receiving a failing grade in the math exam
When thinking of academic prospects and upcoming exams
target_behavior.core_reason: Strong fear of failure and catastrophizing cognitions (one failure equals a ruined future and disappointing the family)
target_behavior.function: Escaping anticipated failure and shame, trying to lower uncertainty through control and vigilance
target_behavior.consequence: Difficulty concentrating, decreased learning motivation, sleep and diet disturbance, overall academic performance declining further

target_behavior.behavior: Social avoidance (distancing from friends and family, less communication)
antecedent: Being asked about exams and grades
Thinking about sharing academic troubles with others or seeking support
target_behavior.core_reason: Not wanting to be a burden on others, fearing others' disappointment or judgment
target_behavior.function: Avoiding negative evaluation and uncomfortable emotions, temporarily lowering anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Increased sense of isolation, reduced social support, worsened anxiety and helplessness
